clue.text: Representative character from book of James

definitions.meaning: an envoy who stands for their country abroad
Henry James wrote the novel The ..., so one of its title figures fits

explanation.walkthrough: 'book of James' sounds biblical, but it is Henry James's novel The Ambassadors.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent to represent a state at a foreign court is a diplomat of top rank.

clue.text: An aromatic flavouring mostly used in meat jelly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: spice is an aromatic flavouring

explanation.surface: A cook adds an aromatic seasoning to a savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of SPICE, leaving SPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to glaze or set cold dishes.

clue.text: Bleat about street needing repair in part of London

indicators.note: about means the bleating sound goes round the other letters

parts.note: baa is the bleat of a sheep

indicators.note: a thing needing repair is broken, so these letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: Sheep complain about a run-down road in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleat' looks like a verb of complaint but is the sheep's noise; 'needing repair' makes TTERSE and 'about' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district on the south bank of the Thames, known for its power station and dogs' home.

clue.text: Variety of cranks pose 'ere? Right

indicators.note: a variety of things is a mixed assortment, so these letters come in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: All sorts of eccentrics strike attitudes here, a cockney asks, and gets agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers' Corner in London's Hyde Park is where anyone may stand up and harangue passers-by, so the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hyde Park spot where soapbox orators, many of them eccentrics, hold forth to the public.

clue.text: Do some drawing in pamphlet, at first

indicators.note: first means the little word at comes before the other piece

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone sketches inside a leaflet before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do some drawing' means draw in, as a magnet draws metal, not sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull towards oneself, which is what a magnet or a charm does.

clue.text: Weigh down with work and urgency of business

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
the press of business is its pressure or urgency

explanation.surface: Someone is burdened by their job and the rush of commercial demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden or crush someone, as a tyrant does to a people.

clue.text: Young group's state

parts.note: Brigham Young led the Mormons west, and their settlement became a US state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Young' looks like an adjective for youth; it is Brigham Young, the Mormon leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The western US state settled by Mormon pioneers under Brigham Young around Salt Lake.

clue.text: Present expression of sympathy

definitions.meaning: in attendance, as in all present and correct
said in comfort, as in a doubled '..., ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Being on the scene means being present; and 'there, there' soothes someone upset.

clue.text: Careful management from partner reduced transport business

parts.note: a husband is a marriage partner
RY is the short form of railway, a transport business

explanation.surface: A spouse runs a scaled-down haulage firm thriftily.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is thrifty stewardship of resources, especially in farming.

clue.text: One who's sceptical, but changes during performance with poet

indicators.note: during means the jumbled piece sits within the performance

parts.note: doing is the performance of an action

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the little word are rearranged

parts.note: Dylan Thomas was a Welsh poet

explanation.surface: A doubter alters his objections while reading verse alongside a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' reads as a conjunction yet is the fodder: 'changes' makes UBT, and 'during' sets it in the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle who refused to believe in the Resurrection without proof, hence any habitual sceptic.

clue.text: Job certainly was invalid

definitions.meaning: the biblical Job is proverbial for his long-suffering endurance
a sick person under a doctor's care

explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' is the biblical figure, not employment, and 'invalid' is the noun for a sick person.
explanation.definitionFit: Job's forbearance is legendary; a person receiving medical treatment is also so called.

clue.text: Valour in the thick of battle, hiding sign of pain

indicators.note: hiding means the cry is concealed within the other word

parts.note: the press is the thick of a fight, where the crowd is densest
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A soldier is brave amid the fighting, concealing any hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is skill and daring, especially in fighting.

clue.text: Conclusive move on board to restrain ship's officer

parts.note: to check is to restrain
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A decisive action is taken aboard to hold back a senior sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the move that traps the king and ends the game.

clue.text: Brought up near a city in Europe

indicators.note: near means the little word sits right beside the other piece

parts.note: bred means raised or brought up

explanation.surface: Someone was raised close to a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Breda is a city in the southern Netherlands.

clue.text: More sensible to use old-fashioned way, right?

parts.note: wise is an archaic word for way or manner, as in 'in no wise'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the traditional method is the smarter one.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning prudent or showing good judgment.

clue.text: Part of US is seen in western with criminals in

parts.note: cons are convicts

explanation.surface: A region of America appears in a cowboy film full of outlaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' looks like a cowboy film but gives just W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Submitted to trial, provided one gets caught and witnessed

indicators.note: gets caught means the pair is trapped inside the longer word

parts.note: tested means put to the test
if means provided that
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A defendant went to court, gave evidence and was snared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submitted to trial' sounds like a court case, but it means put to the test; 'gets caught' sets IFI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to give evidence, so testified means bore witness.

clue.text: Make do and mend around island

indicators.note: around means the longer word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to improve is to make better, to mend

explanation.surface: A castaway gets by and patches things up on their island.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to manage with whatever is at hand.

clue.text: Views, say, with headlands

indicators.note: say means the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: views as a verb means sees
capes are headlands

explanation.surface: Coastal pictures, for instance, featuring promontories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a soundalike of the verb in 'Views', a spelling for the ocean. The whole clue also describes the answer: coastal pictures with headlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings or vistas of the sea, often with cliffs and promontories in them.

clue.text: Instrument little used in Italy

explanation.definitionFit: A small flute pitched an octave higher; the word is Italian for small.

clue.text: Son selected, took part in boat race

parts.note: culled means picked out or selected

explanation.surface: A boy was picked to row in a regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to row with a pair of oars, as in a racing boat.

clue.text: Nomad wants animal back before end of this year

indicators.note: before means the turned animal comes ahead of what follows
back means the word for the animal is read from right to left

parts.note: a pig is an animal

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A traveller wants a pet back before the year is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PIG into GIP; 'end of this' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: An old spelling for a member of the travelling Romani people, a wanderer.

clue.text: Take place of commander, calling up reserves initially

parts.note: OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An officer stands in for his superior by summoning reservists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take place of' looks like substitution, but 'Take place' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen.

clue.text: Manager who works at stock exchange?

definitions.meaning: someone who copes, who manages well
an old word for a horse dealer, trading livestock

explanation.walkthrough: 'stock exchange' is not the City but the trading of horses, the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: One who handles difficulty well; also an old term for a dealer in horses.

clue.text: Detected doing something wrong, and arrested abroad

parts.note: caught means arrested
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: A criminal is found misbehaving and nabbed overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exposed in a mistake or misdeed.

clue.text: Two chaps briefly recorded the minutes, say

parts.note: Tim is short for Timothy
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A pair of men quickly took notes at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded the minutes' suggests a secretary, but it is a stopwatch recording time.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring how long something took, in minutes for instance, is clocking it.

clue.text: Drink more rum, number one

parts.note: sup means to drink

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so these letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A boss orders another round of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is not the drink but an old word for odd, rearranging MORE to REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, the boss.

clue.text: Scholar in one version of Islam or oriental religion

indicators.note: in means the scholar's letters go inside the other piece
version of means a different arrangement of the word's letters

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: An academic is drawn to one form of Islam or an Eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' makes LAISM, and 'in' sets the scholar inside it; 'one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamaism is the Tibetan form of Buddhism, led by lamas.

clue.text: Standard choice between central characters

indicators.note: between means the choosing word goes between the two letters

parts.note: M and N are the letters at the very centre of the alphabet
or expresses a choice

explanation.surface: A typical option between the main figures in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central characters' are not people in a story but M and N, the middle letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is an accepted standard or usual pattern.

clue.text: Be patronising about scrambled second goal

parts.note: C, for circa, means about

indicators.note: scrambled means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football pundit looks down on a messy second score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' rearranges SECOND to ONDESC.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to behave with an air of superiority towards others.
